name: De Vinne Italic 8pt 1900
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office and American Type Founders; the collective ATF page credits Central Type Foundry for the design
description: Eight-point De Vinne Italic with flared serifs, a descending Q tail, double-storey a and g, and complete observed alphabets and figures.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures. Space has a modern layout advance. No punctuation, aliases or invented companions. The date identifies the retained complete census alphabet, supplemented by matching earlier ATF impressions.
observed: The census specimen shows both complete eight-point alphabets and all ten figures. Matching New York and BYU ATF impressions supply clearer letters and figures. Other retained ATF pages document repeated samples and source-quality comparisons. The John Ryan Foundry 1894 specimen, printed page 69, supplies a clearer whole eight-point g from Tumbling.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform scaling within each physical source, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. The historical italic slant is retained. The j uses explicit neighbour isolation. A named lining R preserves a repeated ATF variant alongside the default descending census R. No independent width stretching or cross-size substitution.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: Complete observed alphabets and figures, plus one named lining R alternative through ss01. Four retained native pages supply 63 selected outlines; four further native pages supply comparison evidence. Exact four-times derivatives, uniform source scales, measured row rotations and j neighbour isolation are reproducible. No visible form is drawn or borrowed from another size. See source/METHOD.md. Whole-form source comparisons, measured capital scale and text baseline are retained in source/italic-quality-review.json. Only g changes; its 733-unit advance and all feature mappings are preserved.
